declared.title: The eyewitness post identification feedback effect 15 years later: Theoretical and policy implications.
declared.foundIn: OpenAlex search « eyewitness post-identification feedback effect 15 years later meta-analysis » (2026-11-23)

population: about 7,000 participant-witnesses in lab experiments from the United States, Canada, Europe and Australia

findings.text: Telling witnesses « good, you picked the suspect » robustly inflates what they later report: their certainty, how well they saw, their attention…, with large effects overall

support.sentence: The results show that confirming feedback robustly inflates eyewitnesses' retrospective judgments across experimental manipulations and laboratory settings with large effect sizes.

limits: the number of studies and the effect sizes are in the full text (not read): « large » is the authors' word, said of all the judgements together, not of certainty alone
lab experiments on lineup identification; the feedback came from the person running the lineup
no sample from the Middle East or North Africa
